text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- Prime Minister Gyula Horn nominated Szabolcs Fazekas to replace dismissed Industry and Trade Minister Tamas Suchman, Judit Csiha, political state secretary at the Ministry of Justice, to the post of Privatisation Minister and Arpad Kovacs, a director in the State Audit Office, to the post of chairman of the State Privatisation and Holding Co.'s (APV) board of management.
- National Bank President Gyorgy Suranyi said that September inflation was 1.5-1.7 per cent, half a percentage point less than in the same month last year.

- The first Hungarian credit-rating institute will begin operating within a year according to a cooperation agreement signed yesterday by the Hungarian Federation of Banks and the American agency USAID.
- The Swiss firm Compagnie Financiere Michelin yesterday signed the contract to buy the rubber manufacturer Taurus.
- A small bomb exploded near the Great Synagogue on Dohany utca last night, causing only minimal damage and no injuries.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- The redeployment of US IFOR troops withdrawing from Bosnia to their temporary bases in south Hungary will start within days.
- President Arpad Goncz said that the reiteration of the border issue is life-threatening for Hungary, and weakens Hungarian foreign policy.
- Sandor Puskas, chairman of the Supervisory Board of APV said that the prime minister personally assured him on Tuesday that he had dropped a plan to remove the members of the board.
- Young Democrat Zsolt Nemeth complained before regular business in Parliament that ethnic Hungarians in Slovakia are being exposed to continuous discrimination.
- Tuesday's auction of one-month treasury bills attracted demand of HUF 1.5 billion whereas the value of the papers offered was HUF 1 billion.

- A general meeting of the refrigeration company Goldsun (major owners: Israeli company Sunfrost and US-based Shamrock) will probably decide tomorrow whether to liquidate the firm or to increase its capital.
VILAGGAZDASAG

- Despite APV lawyers advised that the tender was not valid, APV and Acel XXI Kft, managers of the Dunaferr Rt steelworks, signed a contract featuring a HUF 1 billion incentive fee last Thursday evening, the day before the APV management was sacked.
- Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek will visit Hungary on October 15.
- The continuous increase in the price of fodder and related services could ruin the field of animal breeding, warned a report by the Agricultural Ministry.
- HUF 2.65 billion from next year's budget will be spent on developments promoting the country's membership in the European Union, said Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy.
NEPSZABADSAG
- President Arpad Goncz will pay an official visit to Turkey October 16-18.

- Foreign Ministry political state secretary Istvan Szent-Ivanyi said that there could be closer cooperation between Italy, Slovenia and Hungary on EuroAtlantic integration and infrastructural and economic ties.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- Nearly 9,000 tonnes of tobacco were produced this year.
-- Budapest newsroom (36-1) 327 4040
